verdict.rationale: kitty's configuration lives in plain-text kitty.conf files that users own directly and the project itself is open-source, so there's no vendor lock-in and settings can be copied/ported freely, and remote-control scripting exposes window/session state as JSON. However there's no dedicated 'export my data' feature (e.g., session history, scrollback, or theme export as a documented bulk-export tool) beyond the inherent plain-text config files. missing for 10: explicit documented export/import of scrollback or session data, migration tooling, and independent confirmation that users treat config portability as a full data-export solution.
